correctness.rationale: For nonzero rank-one X, its two-sided annihilator is the line of the complementary projector when trace(X)≠0, or the line spanned by X when trace(X)=0. This forces any solution into axes, pair projector components, or one common nilpotent cone. The projector component is irreducible with dense open parametrized by an ordered pair of distinct projective lines and two nonzero eigenvalue scalars and an explicit degeneration of nilpotent boundaries; the cone is the Segre–Veronese affine cone. Generic witnesses prove all components maximal and yield the sharp dimensional threshold. Counting by exact nonzero support establishes the point/motivic formulas. The independent-entry finite-field program reproduces all 27 point-count cases plus three complete support classifications. The nonreduced equation scheme is not claimed reduced.

evidence: Schröer, arXiv:math/0211293, introduction, identifies all rank-stratified components for the unrestricted pair variety Z(n), and the body treats nilpotent pairs V(n,a,b).

Huisgen-Zimmermann and Goodearl, arXiv:1108.2833, study representation varieties with projective parametrizations and provide the Carlson example, not all m-variable coordinate-cross representations at rank two.

The classification of all-square-zero matrix tuples imposes X_i^2=0 for every index and treats a strict sublocus of this representation variety; its formulas cannot count the nonnilpotent rank-one complementary-projector tuples or the axis components.

Kinser–Lőrincz, arXiv:1810.10997, studies node splitting where every two-arrow path through a node is zero. The one-vertex multi-loop algebra here retains every individual loop square, so its vertex is not a node, and the paper does not state the present exact component or all-field tuple enumeration.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Schröer has stronger matrix-size coverage but only two simultaneous matrices. The general module-variety framework has greater categorical scope but supplies methods rather than the explicit component count and threshold for the algebra family treated here. No direct implication to the complete multi-arity result was found. The square-zero-only tuple theory gives the common-nilpotent locus here, but leaves all nonnilpotent configurations, the total component decomposition, and the all-tuple count unresolved. The node-splitting theorems do not directly apply because the coordinate-axis fibre-product algebra allows arbitrarily high powers of each loop.

originality.rationale: The primary literature establishes strong pair results and general representation-variety methods, which are explicitly excluded from novelty; neither the located pair literature nor the inspected finite-dimensional representation-variety examples gives the all-arity, dimension-two component transition or higher-arity point/motivic formulas. Searches of equivalences, broader methods, matrix-annihilator graph cliques and prior published records located no implication to the complete new statement. Priority is provisional due to possible unindexed multibranch results.
residual_risks: Historical index coverage is incomplete; a multi-branch module-variety or zero-product graph clique theorem under different terminology might imply the present statements.
Some general representation-variety techniques can derive special cases after nontrivial specialization; the explicit all-arity formula and geometric threshold were not found in the inspected text.
All prior comparisons are same-author literature inspection, not independent publication-priority certification.

value.rationale: The fibre product of affine lines is a canonical reducible curve algebra, and its fixed-rank representation varieties are natural invariants. An all-arity classification identifies a new component at three independent generators and exact failure of equidimensionality at four, along with explicit finite-field and motivic census for arbitrary tuple length. The significance does not rely on a small arbitrary cutoff or computation alone: it is a sharp structural change with implications for multi-branch representation geometry and point-counting.
